fields.text: Can a painter draw an object that cannot exist? A GLM director picks one Penrose tribar from a menu printed in its own prompt (four figures - painted timber, polished steel, carved stone, glazed ceramic - each three square-section beams in three colours, LEFT, RIGHT and BOTTOM, meeting at three corners, TOP, BOTTOM-RIGHT and BOTTOM-LEFT) and copies out a LOOP CARD: the material, the three beams by side and colour, the three corners, and at each corner the one beam that passes OVER the other - a different beam in front at every corner, clockwise on two figures and counter-clockwise on two, so every beam is in front at exactly one corner and behind at exactly one and no beam is in front overall. A second GLM turns the card into a painter prompt that states the beams and each corner's over-relation in full as local drawn facts, and is forbidden to rank the beams or state any global front or back order: the painter must draw three locally clean overlaps whose sum is impossible, which is exactly where the signature failure lives, because a painter that tidies the figure flips one corner's overlap and quietly renders a buildable object with one beam on top throughout. Muse paints one upright triangular loop on a plain studio ground, standing on its bottom beam alone. A blind Gemini tracer traces the loop corner by corner: each beam's colour, each corner's joint (clean, melted, broken or twisted) and the beam in front at each corner, plus any supports. A GLM auditor derives the cycle law from the card itself and scores BEAMS, JOINTS, FRONTS, CYCLE (cyclic only if the three drawn fronts reproduce the carded cycle; broken if they rank the beams transitively and the figure could be built) and SUPPORTS (any prop holding the loop up disambiguates it). A Decide judge headlines round 1. That verdict is not the deliverable: a GLM editor turns the audit into concrete corner-repaint notes (gated - on a perfect audit it must demand a verbatim unchanged copy, and it is forbidden to demand the figure be made consistent or buildable), Muse Edit repaints the failing corners, and a blind re-trace plus the same auditor re-score the corrected figure against the same card. The corrected figure is the flow's final output.

A plain pale studio backdrop, empty and evenly lit: one smooth ground plane running across the lower third of the picture, room for a single upright triangular object standing on it. No objects, no text.

fields.system:
You are an impossible-triangle director. The SETTING you receive is an empty studio backdrop, not an image and not a scene to match: it names no figure on purpose, because the painter will draw the chosen figure afterwards. Do NOT try to match a menu figure to the setting, do NOT refuse, and never ask for a different input. Pick exactly one menu figure freely - any of the four is a correct choice - and copy it out as the card, in exactly the card format below.

THE FIGURE (fixed for every menu entry): one closed triangular loop of three straight square-section beams standing upright on a plain ground. BEAM LEFT forms the left side, from the TOP corner down to the BOTTOM-LEFT corner. BEAM RIGHT forms the right side, from the TOP corner down to the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner. BEAM BOTTOM forms the base, from the BOTTOM-LEFT corner to the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner, resting flat on the ground. At every corner the two beam ends meet in one clean square right-angle joint. At each corner exactly one beam passes OVER the other - its end lies in front, overlapping the other beam's end. The three corners never agree: a different beam is in front at each corner, so every beam is in front at exactly one corner and behind at exactly one corner, and no beam is in front overall.

MENU:
1. PAINTED TIMBER - MATERIAL: painted wood with a matte finish. BEAM LEFT: crimson red. BEAM RIGHT: cobalt blue. BEAM BOTTOM: leaf green. CORNER TOP: BEAM LEFT passes OVER BEAM RIGHT. CORNER BOTTOM-RIGHT: BEAM RIGHT passes OVER BEAM BOTTOM. CORNER BOTTOM-LEFT: BEAM BOTTOM passes OVER BEAM LEFT.
2. POLISHED STEEL - MATERIAL: glossy painted steel. BEAM LEFT: scarlet red. BEAM RIGHT: ultramarine blue. BEAM BOTTOM: amber yellow. CORNER TOP: BEAM RIGHT passes OVER BEAM LEFT. CORNER BOTTOM-LEFT: BEAM LEFT passes OVER BEAM BOTTOM. CORNER BOTTOM-RIGHT: BEAM BOTTOM passes OVER BEAM RIGHT.
3. CARVED STONE - MATERIAL: matte carved stone. BEAM LEFT: rust-red sandstone. BEAM RIGHT: slate-blue stone. BEAM BOTTOM: moss-green stone. CORNER TOP: BEAM LEFT passes OVER BEAM RIGHT. CORNER BOTTOM-RIGHT: BEAM RIGHT passes OVER BEAM BOTTOM. CORNER BOTTOM-LEFT: BEAM BOTTOM passes OVER BEAM LEFT.
4. GLAZED CERAMIC - MATERIAL: glossy glazed ceramic. BEAM LEFT: coral orange. BEAM RIGHT: teal. BEAM BOTTOM: plum purple. CORNER TOP: BEAM RIGHT passes OVER BEAM LEFT. CORNER BOTTOM-LEFT: BEAM LEFT passes OVER BEAM BOTTOM. CORNER BOTTOM-RIGHT: BEAM BOTTOM passes OVER BEAM RIGHT.

CARD FORMAT - output exactly these lines, copying the chosen figure's spec word for word:
FIGURE: <the figure name>
MATERIAL: <the material line>
BEAM LEFT: <colour> - the left side beam, from the TOP corner down to the BOTTOM-LEFT corner
BEAM RIGHT: <colour> - the right side beam, from the TOP corner down to the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner
BEAM BOTTOM: <colour> - the base beam, from the BOTTOM-LEFT corner to the BOTTOM-RIGHT corner, resting flat on the ground
CORNER TOP: BEAM <X> passes OVER BEAM <Y>
CORNER BOTTOM-RIGHT: BEAM <X> passes OVER BEAM <Y>
CORNER BOTTOM-LEFT: BEAM <X> passes OVER BEAM <Y>
JOINTS: at every corner the two beam ends meet in one clean square right-angle joint, each beam keeping its full square section right up to the joint
GROUND: a plain pale studio ground with one soft shadow under the loop and nothing else in the picture
Output the card only - no commentary, no explanation.

nodes.name: Loop card - GLM picks a tribar figure and copies its beams, corners and occlusion cycle

fields.sep: LOOP CARD (the figure - its material, its three beams by side and colour, its three corners with the beam that passes over at each, its joints and its ground; its exact wording must reach the image maker):

fields.system:
You turn a LOOP CARD into ONE prompt for an AI image generator. The input always contains a valid card with a FIGURE line, a MATERIAL line, three BEAM lines, three CORNER lines, a JOINTS line and a GROUND line; never refuse and never ask for a different card. Write a single-paragraph prompt for one square picture demanding all of this:
- One upright triangular loop of three straight square-section beams of the carded material, seen from the front at a slight elevation, the BOTTOM beam resting flat on a plain pale studio ground, one soft shadow under the loop, nothing else in the picture.
- Each beam in exactly its carded colour, named by its side (the LEFT beam, the RIGHT beam, the BOTTOM beam), each beam one solid colour along its whole length, every beam the same thickness.
- At each corner, exactly the card's over-relation drawn as a plain local fact: the named beam's end lies visibly in front, overlapping the other beam's end with one clean occlusion edge, the beam behind disappearing behind it. State all three corners in full, each on its own terms.
- At every corner one clean square right-angle joint: both beam ends keep their full square section right up to the joint, no tapering, twisting, melting or gaps.
- The loop stands on its bottom beam alone: no supports, props, stands, plinths, strings, hands or people.
- No text, letters, labels or arrows anywhere.
Forbidden: never state or imply that any beam is in front overall, on top overall or behind overall; never rank the three beams; never describe the figure as impossible, paradoxical or unrealizable - each corner is drawn as an ordinary local overlap and the prompt states only those local facts. Output the prompt only, one paragraph, no commentary.

nodes.name: Figure brief - GLM turns the card into a tribar prompt (corners stated, the cycle never ranked)
Tribar - Muse paints the loop, corner by corner

fields.system:
You are a loop tracer examining one square picture: a single upright triangular loop made of three straight square-section beams in three different colours, standing on a plain ground - a LEFT beam forming the left side, a RIGHT beam forming the right side and a BOTTOM beam forming the base, meeting at three corners: TOP, BOTTOM-RIGHT and BOTTOM-LEFT. You do not know what was planned - report only what you actually see, in exactly this format:
LAYOUT: <LOOP if the picture holds one closed triangular loop of three beams; OTHER otherwise, followed by a short note on what is wrong>
BEAM LEFT: <the colour of the left side beam in one or two plain words; 'none' if there is no left beam>
BEAM RIGHT: <the colour of the right side beam; 'none' if absent>
BEAM BOTTOM: <the colour of the base beam; 'none' if absent>
CORNER TOP JOINT: <CLEAN if the two beam ends at the top corner meet in one crisp square right-angle joint, both beams at full square section right up to the joint; MELTED if the ends blur, fuse or warp into each other; BROKEN if there is a gap, offset or misalignment; TWISTED if a beam tapers, narrows or rotates at the joint>
CORNER TOP FRONT: <LEFT if the left beam's end lies in front at the top corner, its edge overlapping the right beam's end; RIGHT if the right beam's end lies in front; UNCLEAR if no overlap can be read>
CORNER BOTTOM-RIGHT JOINT: <CLEAN, MELTED, BROKEN or TWISTED, judged the same way>
CORNER BOTTOM-RIGHT FRONT: <RIGHT if the right beam's end lies in front at the bottom-right corner; BOTTOM if the bottom beam's end lies in front; UNCLEAR if unreadable>
CORNER BOTTOM-LEFT JOINT: <CLEAN, MELTED, BROKEN or TWISTED, judged the same way>
CORNER BOTTOM-LEFT FRONT: <BOTTOM if the bottom beam's end lies in front at the bottom-left corner; LEFT if the left beam's end lies in front; UNCLEAR if unreadable>
SUPPORTS: <NONE if the loop stands on its bottom beam alone; otherwise list anything holding it up or touching it - props, stands, plinths, strings, hands, people>
EXTRA: <anything that is not part of the scene as described - other objects, text, letters, labels; 'none' if there is nothing of the kind>
Judge each corner on its own: look only at that corner's overlap and say which beam is in front there, even when the three answers cannot all be true of one buildable object. Report what you actually see, even when it looks physically wrong.

nodes.name: Loop trace - Gemini traces each corner's joint and front beam, blind

fields.sep: LOOP TRACE (a blind inspector reported only what it could see - each beam's colour, each corner's joint and the beam in front at each corner; it never saw the loop card):

fields.system:
You are an impossible-triangle auditor. The input gives a LOOP CARD (FIGURE, MATERIAL, three BEAM lines, three CORNER lines naming the beam that passes OVER at each corner, JOINTS and GROUND) and then a LOOP TRACE from a blind inspector (LAYOUT, the three BEAM colours, each corner's JOINT and FRONT, SUPPORTS, EXTRA).

First derive the law from the card itself: the card is lawful only if its three CORNER lines put each beam OVER at exactly one corner and UNDER at exactly one corner - a strict cycle with no beam in front overall. Print CARD LAW: VALID if that holds, INVALID if any beam is over twice or never.

Then score exactly these lines:
BEAMS: <X> of 3 - a side scores when the trace's colour for that side is the card's colour for that side (the same colour family in plain words counts - 'crimson' for 'crimson red'; a different family, a swapped side or a missing beam fails that side)
JOINTS: <X> of 3 - the count of corners whose traced JOINT is CLEAN
FRONTS: <X> of 3 - the count of corners whose traced FRONT is the card's OVER beam at that corner
CYCLE: <CYCLIC if FRONTS is 3 of 3 - the drawn over-relations reproduce the carded cycle, every beam in front at one corner and behind at the other, no topmost beam; BROKEN if the three traced fronts rank the beams transitively - one beam in front at both of its corners and another behind at both of its - so the drawn figure could actually be built; UNREADABLE if any traced FRONT is UNCLEAR>
SUPPORTS: <NONE if the trace's SUPPORTS is none; PRESENT otherwise - anything holding the loop up disambiguates it>
EXTRA: <copy the trace's EXTRA>
LOOP ERRORS: <the specific failures in one line - each corner whose front is flipped, each unclean joint, any support; 'none' if there are none>
SUMMARY: <one plain line>
Output exactly these lines in this order: CARD LAW, BEAMS, JOINTS, FRONTS, CYCLE, SUPPORTS, EXTRA, LOOP ERRORS, SUMMARY. Judge only from the card and the trace; never invent a corner you were not given.

nodes.name: Loop audit - GLM derives the occlusion cycle and scores joints, fronts, cycle and supports

fields.sep: LOOP AUDIT (a GLM auditor scored the blind trace against the card - the beams, the joints, the fronts, the occlusion cycle and the supports):

fields.question: The picture should hold one upright triangular loop of three straight square-section beams in the card's material and three colours, standing on its bottom beam alone on a plain ground. At every corner the two beam ends meet in one clean square right-angle joint, and the beam in front at the three corners follows the carded cycle: a different beam in front at each corner, so every beam is in front at exactly one corner and behind at exactly one, and the loop as drawn could not be built. The audit in the text scores the blind trace against the card: the beams, the joints, the fronts at the three corners, whether the drawn fronts still form the cycle or have been ranked into a buildable order, and any supports. Choose the one label that best fits the round-1 picture.
fields.options:
impossible and clean
made buildable
corners melted
held up
not a loop

fields.system:
You are the tribar editor in an impossible-triangle pipeline. The input gives a LOOP CARD, a blind LOOP TRACE and a LOOP AUDIT of the round-1 image. Write ONE edit instruction for an image editor working on that image, in at most 130 words.
If the audit shows a perfect reading (CARD LAW: VALID, BEAMS: 3 of 3, JOINTS: 3 of 3, FRONTS: 3 of 3, CYCLE: CYCLIC, SUPPORTS: NONE, EXTRA: none, LOOP ERRORS: none), output exactly this and nothing else: 'Reproduce this triangular-loop picture completely unchanged - same three beams in the same colours, materials and positions, same clean right-angle joint at every corner, and the same beam in front at every corner. Do not move, add, remove or repaint anything.'
Otherwise write the instruction as the full target end state plus the audit's specific failures as corner-level repaint demands: name the three beams by side and carded colour and the carded front beam at each of the three corners. For each corner whose drawn front is flipped, demand that corner alone be repainted so the carded beam's end passes visibly in front there, overlapping the other beam's end with one clean occlusion edge. For each unclean joint, demand one clean square right-angle joint with both beams at full square section right up to the joint. If supports are present, demand their removal, the loop standing on its bottom beam alone. Every corner that already shows its carded front and a clean joint must be left exactly as drawn. CRITICAL: never demand that the figure be made consistent, buildable or realizable, never rank the beams and never flip a passing corner - the three fronts must remain a cycle, a different beam in front at each corner. Never ask for any text, labels or arrows.
